subject: working on a a list of species

messages.author: 9c3183af58028473
messages.subject: working on a a list of species
parts:
Juergen

We continue to use your great package - I am most impressed with your generous support to the camtrapR community.

What would be really neat would be to use several of your functions to work on a set of species. Eg dectionHistory which has a Species argument. The vingette examples just give a single species. But it would be great if one could give the function a set of of species, c("Red Fox", "Species1", "Species2", ...).  So far we have been using a for loop to cycle through a list of species or manually copying the function, each copy with a different species argument.

There are number of functions where this would be a big help.  Eg
spatialDetectionHistory
detectionMaps

Is this possible? Sensible?

David

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: working on a a list of species
parts:
Hi David,
that's an interesting idea, but I am not sure it is really needed. Like you said, one can achieve that with a for loop, or maybe even better, lapply(). That would at least save you the manual copying. 
detectionMaps will automatically plot all species, unless you specify the parameter "speciesToShow". For detectionHistory, you can use lapply like this: 

data(camtraps)
data(recordTableSample)

camop_no_problem <- cameraOperation(CTtable      = camtraps,
                                    stationCol   = "Station",
                                    setupCol     = "Setup_date",
                                    retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date",
                                    hasProblems  = FALSE,
                                    dateFormat   = "%d/%m/%Y"
)

species <- c("PBE", "VTA")

list_dh <- lapply(species, FUN = detectionHistory, 
                  recordTable     = recordTableSample,
                  camOp           = camop_no_problem,
                  occasionLength  = 7,
                  day1            = "station",
                  includeEffort   = TRUE, 
                  scaleEffort     = FALSE
)
names(list_dh) <- species

> list_dh
$PBE
$PBE$detection_history
         o1 o2 o3 o4 o5 o6 o7
StationA  0  0  1  1  0  1  0
StationB  1  1  0  1  0  1  0
StationC  1  1  1  0  1  0  0

$PBE$effort
          o1 o2 o3 o4 o5 o6  o7
StationA 6.5  7  7  7  7  7 0.5
StationB 6.5  7  7  7  7  7 1.5
StationC 6.5  7  7  7  7  7 1.5


$VTA
$VTA$detection_history
         o1 o2 o3 o4 o5 o6 o7
StationA  0  1  0  0  1  0  0
StationB  0  1  0  1  0  0  0
StationC  0  0  1  0  0  0  0

$VTA$effort
          o1 o2 o3 o4 o5 o6  o7
StationA 6.5  7  7  7  7  7 0.5
StationB 6.5  7  7  7  7  7 1.5
StationC 6.5  7  7  7  7  7 1.5


# accessing one species
list_dh$PBE

# and the detection / effort matrices of one species
list_dh$PBE$detection_history
list_dh$PBE$effort

Would that work for you?
Best regards,
Jürgen
